children.text: gandhāḍhyāsau bhuvanaviditā ketakī svarṇavarṇā padmabhrāntyā kṣudhitamadhupaḥ puṣpamadhye papāta
children.translated_text: Rich in fragrance, known throughout the world, and golden in color was that screw-pine flower; mistaking it for a lotus, a hungry bee fell into the midst of the blossom.

children.text: andhībhūtaḥ kusumarajasā kaṇṭakaiś chinnapakṣaḥ sthātuṃ gantuṃ dvayamapi sakhe naiva śakto dvirephaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Blinded by the flower's pollen and with his wings cut by its thorns, the bee, my friend, was able neither to remain nor to depart.

children.text: gandhāḍhyāṃ navamallikāṃ madhukarastyaktvā gato yūthikāṃ daivāttāṃ ca vihāya campakavanaṃ paścāt sarojaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoning a fragrant fresh jasmine, a bee went to a yūthikā jasmine; by fate he left that too, then went to a grove of campaka trees, and afterward to a lotus.

children.text: baddhastatra niśākareṇa vidhinā krandatyasau mūḍhadhīḥ saṃtoṣeṇa vinā parābhavapadaṃ prāpnoti mūḍho janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Trapped there by fate when the moon arose, that foolish creature cries out. Without contentment, a foolish person comes to a state of humiliation.

children.text: ye'mī te mukulodgamādanudinaṃ tvāmāśritāḥ ṣaṭpadāste bhrāmyanti phalādvavahir bahirato dṛṣṭvā na sambhāṣase
children.translated_text: Those six-footed bees who have depended on you every day since your buds first appeared now wander outside your fruit; therefore, although you see them, you do not speak to them.

children.text: ye kīṭāstava dṛkpathaṃ ca na gatāste tvatphalābhyantare dhik tvāṃ cūta yataḥ parāparaparijñānānabhijño bhavān ||
children.translated_text: The worms that never even entered your field of vision are inside your fruit. Shame on you, mango tree, for you do not understand the distinction between superior and inferior.

children.text: nītaṃ janma navīnanīrajavane pītaṃ madhu svecchayā mālatyāḥ kusumeṣu yena satataṃ kelī kṛtā helayā
children.translated_text: He who spent his life in a grove of fresh lotuses, drank nectar at will, and continually sported without restraint among jasmine flowers—

children.text: teneyaṃ madhugandhalubdhamanasā guñjālatāṃ sevyate hā dhig daivakṛtaṃ sa eva madhupaḥ kāṃ kāṃ daśāṃ nāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that very bee, his mind now craving the scent of honey, attends upon a guñjā creeper. Alas, shame on what fate has wrought! What condition has that bee not undergone?
Mistaking a parrot's beak for a palāśa flower, a bee
alights upon it; and the parrot, mistaking him for a jambu fruit, seeks to kill him.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sphīto bhavadalirasau lekhyapadmaṃ viśālaṃ citraṃ citraṃ kimiti kimiti vyāharan niṣpapāta
children.translated_text: On seeing a vast painted lotus, that bee grew excited and flew down, repeatedly exclaiming, “How marvelous! How marvelous! What is this? What is this?”

children.text: nāsmin gandho na ca madhukaṇā nāsti tatsaukumāryaṃ ghūrṇanmūrdhnā bata nataśirā vrīḍayā nirjagāma ||
children.translated_text: There was no fragrance in it, no drops of nectar, nor any of a lotus's delicacy. Alas, reeling his head and hanging it low, he departed in shame.
That bee, beloved of the lotus grove and a connoisseur of playful delights among clusters of night-blooming lilies,
having arrived in a foreign land under the power of fate, sets great store by the nectar of a kuṭaja flower.

children.text: rātrirgamiṣyati bhaviṣyati suprabhātaṃ bhāsvānudeṣyati hasiṣyati padmajālam
children.translated_text: “The night will pass, a beautiful dawn will come, the sun will rise, and the mass of lotuses will open”—

children.text: itthaṃ vicintayati kośagate dvirephe hā hanta hanta nalinīṃ gaja ujjahāra ||
children.translated_text: while the bee enclosed in the calyx was thinking in this way, alas, alas, an elephant uprooted the lotus.
